TypeIV_Study.definition: Skin which is light brown and it rarely burns when exposed to the sun. It is usually seen in people of Mediterranean origin.

TypeV_Study.definition: Skin which is brown and it burns very rarely when exposed to the sun. It is usually seen in people of Middle Eastern origin.

TypeVI_Study.definition: Skin which is dark brown or black and it never burns when exposed to the sun.

Combination_Study.definition: A skin condition which features two or more different skin types on the face, and the condition of your skin may fluctuate between seasons.

EpidermalMelasma_Study.definition: Categorical measure of epidermal melasma (where melanin is in the more superficial layers of the skin).

MixedMelasma_Study.definition: Categorical measure of the combination of dermal and epidermal melasma.

Whole Genome Sequencing_Study.definition: A procedure that can determine the DNA sequence for nearly the entire genome of an individual.

RNA Sequencing_Study.definition: An assay that determines the sequence of an RNA molecule.

Variant Calling_Study.definition: Detect, identify and map mutations, such as single nucleotide polymorphisms, short indels and structural variants, in multiple DNA sequences. Flow Cytometry_Study.definition: A technique for counting, examining and sorting microscopic particles suspended in a stream of fluid.

Mass Spectrometry_Study.definition: An analytical technique wherein ions are separated according to their ratio of charge to mass. From the mass spectrum produced, the atomic weight of the particle can be deduced.

Microarray_Study.definition: Analysis using microarray technology (e.g., cDNA arrays to see gene expression or protein microarrays to profile the pattern of proteins).

Genomics_Study.definition: The study of comprehensive sets of genes via high throughput methods.

Transcriptomics_Study.definition: The analysis of transcriptomes, or a set of all the RNA molecules in a specific cell, tissue etc.

Metabolomics_Study.definition: The systematic study of metabolites, the chemical processes they are involved, and the chemical fingerprints of specific cellular processes in a whole cell, tissue, organ or organism.

Lipidomics_Study.definition: A study of the complete set of lipids produced in a given cell or organism under specific conditions.

Proteomics_Study.definition: The global analysis of cellular proteins. Proteomics uses a combination of sophisticated techniques including two-dimensional (2D) gel electrophoresis, image analysis, mass spectrometry, amino acid sequencing, and bio-informatics to resolve comprehensively, to quantify, and to characterize proteins. The application of proteomics provides major opportunities to elucidate disease mechanisms and to identify new diagnostic markers and therapeutic targets.

Epigenetics_Study.definition: Epigenetics is the study of the chemical modification of specific genes or gene-associated proteins of an organism.

FabricSwatch_Study.alt_definition: Swatch of fabric placed inside a T-shirt that is worn by a consumer to measure skin microbiome that is transferred to the swatch.

Vagina_Study.definition: The female genital canal, extending from the uterus to the vulva.
Vagina_Study.alt_definition: The muscular tube leading from the external genitals to the cervix of the uterus in women and most female mammals

HighVagina_Study.alt_definition: A high vaginal swab is a medical procedure performed in obstetrics and gynaecology to test vaginal discharge for the presence of vaginal thrush, bacterial vaginosis and trichomonas vaginalis.

VulvoVagina_Study.alt_definition: A sample taken from or relating to the external female genitals

Ichthyosis_Study.definition: A group of inherited or acquired skin disorders characterized by a dry, thickened, and scaly skin. The skin changes range from mild to severe.
Ichthyosis_Study.alt_definition: A group of skin disorders that lead to dry, itchy skin that appears scaly, rough, and red.

Lamellar Ichthyosis_Study.definition: A very rare, autosomal recessive inherited skin disorder present at birth. It is characterized by the presence of a transparent membrane encasing the newborn. This membrane sheds in about two weeks after birth to reveal generalized scaling and skin erythema.
Lamellar Ichthyosis_Study.alt_definition: People with lamellar ichthyosis typically have large, dark, plate-like scales covering their skin on most of their body.

Epidermolytic Ichthyosis_Study.definition: An autosomal dominant inherited skin disorder caused by mutations in the KRT1 and KRT10 genes. It is manifested at birth and is characterized by generalized erythema, skin blisters and skin fragility.
Epidermolytic Ichthyosis_Study.alt_definition: Epidermolytic ichthyosis (bullous ichthyosiform erythroderma) is a rare autosomal dominant disorder of cornification caused by mutations in keratins 1 and 10

Congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma_St.definition: An ichthyosiform abnormality of the skin with congenital onset.
Congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma_St.alt_definition: This is an extremely rare skin disorder characterised by abnormal scaling of the skin with underlying redness.

Netherton syndrome_Study.definition: Netherton syndrome (NS) is a skin disorder characterized by congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma (CIE), a distinctive hair shaft defect (trichorrhexis invaginata; TI) and atopic manifestations.
Netherton syndrome_Study.alt_definition: Netherton syndrome is a disorder that affects the skin, hair, and immune system. Newborns with Netherton syndrome have skin that is red and scaly (ichthyosiform erythroderma), and the skin may leak fluid.

Urine_Study.definition: The fluid that is excreted by the kidneys. It is stored in the bladder and discharged through the urethra.
